correctness.rationale: The CC-ring commuting graph is a disjoint union of cliques. The domination polynomial is therefore a product of factors \((1+x)^m-1\). After shifting by \(y=1+x\), cyclotomic unique factorization records for each \(d\) the number of component sizes divisible by \(d\); finite Möbius inversion recovers the exact multiplicity of every component size. Direct finite-ring and exhaustive cluster-profile computations corroborate the argument without replacing it.

evidence: Dutta--Nath prove that every finite CC-ring commuting graph is a disjoint union of complete graphs determined by noncentral centralizers.
Alikhani records multiplicativity of domination polynomials over connected components.
Jahari--Alikhani exhibit many nonisomorphic graphs in the D-equivalence class of clique unions.
Later finite-ring commuting-graph work studies spectra and energies rather than domination-polynomial reconstruction.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broad structural ring literature and the broad domination-polynomial equivalence literature were both inspected; their combination does not already state the inversion theorem.

evidence: The CC-ring theorem gives only the clique decomposition and spectral/genus consequences.
The domination-equivalence paper proves that arbitrary nonisomorphic graphs can share the clique-union polynomial, so global D-uniqueness is false.
Multiplicativity gives the product expression but not, by itself, the divisibility inversion recovering all component sizes.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The final claim adds a precise uniqueness statement within the algebraic graph class. It is neither a global D-uniqueness claim nor a restatement of the existing decomposition.

originality.rationale: Inspected sources separately provide the CC-ring clique decomposition, domination-polynomial multiplicativity, and examples of nonisomorphic graphs domination-equivalent to clique unions. None states that the polynomial uniquely recovers the clique profile inside finite CC-ring commuting graphs or gives the cyclotomic inversion used here.
residual_risks: A graph-polynomial paper not indexed under commuting graphs or cluster graphs may contain the same cyclotomic reconstruction observation.
The result is complete only for graph isomorphism within finite CC-ring commuting graphs, not for arbitrary domination-equivalent graphs.
The general theorem does not reconstruct the center size or the ring isomorphism type.

value.rationale: The claim identifies a natural algebraic graph class on which a generally non-complete graph polynomial becomes a complete isomorphism invariant and gives an explicit inversion algorithm. The special \(C_p\times C_p\) quotient family additionally recovers concrete ring data \(p\), \(|Z(R)|\), and \(|R|\).
